summary.intent: Run Session 2 of the v1-alpha launch plan: ship WP D (init boundary: branch-name/YAML handling and workflow-only retry), J's first piece (twine OIDC env), and WP L (publish isolation: split workflows into credential-free package jobs and a credentialed execute job, sealed npm tarballs).
summary.outcome: WP D merged as PR #565 and J's first piece pushed as PR #569, both gated. WP L is implemented and committed in two signed commits (c847b7668 plus a mutant-test follow-up) with the gate green, but mutants have not been re-run, and it has not been pushed, linked to trail #459 or put through ci-pr; #569's docs/changeset are still pending.

repo: Generated workflow templates (simple_workflow.tmpl, matrix_workflow.tmpl) are rendered by init.rs, so WP D, L and J all edit the same files; the rules forbid stacking PRs, so later WPs must wait for the earlier one to merge.
callisto-model has its own Version and identity types (BranchName, CommitSha) re-exported via glob from identity.rs; use them rather than adding a semver dependency to the CLI.
Gate is by exit code: just pre-push, lint, doc-check, test, and just ci; mutation testing is cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <diff> --test-tool nextest.
Error codes are scarce: new codes need lead approval, so existing ones were generalized (E304 for unsupported artifact owners, E306/E308/E309 for seal and build failures).
Commits must be signed with no session trailer and pushed with an explicit refspec, verified with git ls-remote; use EnterWorktree name=<wp>, never path=.
mutants.out*/ is now gitignored (mutants.out.old had been tracked).

cargo package -p a fails when a depends on an unpublished sibling crate of the same release; only the set-wise `cargo package -p a -p b --locked` verifies, so CI uses one credential-free package job and `cargo publish --no-verify`.
Trail findings are managed with `entire trail finding add/list/resolve`; trails link via `entire trail link <n> --base main` and `entire trail ci-pr`.

code.finding: The npm adapter ignored its artifact-manifest argument and published from the checkout; L changes it to publish only the sealed tarball, re-hashed before publish.
Matrix drops artifacts with unsupported owners (e.g. npm), causing release failure 'no entry for artifact slot', hence the E304 rejection on the workflow-only path.
render_init prints a [DRY-RUN] message whenever initialized is false, so the workflow-only report had to set initialized true on a real write.
Promised that native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged; L breaks this (publish-time hooks no longer run), so it needed a Breaking/Action changeset.

workflow: An independent reviewer subagent reading only the source caught real defects (false dry-run label, ignored user config, silently dropped flags) that the green gate missed.
Mutation testing surfaced 20 missed mutants in L's diff; tests were added for 18 and 2 were justified as equivalent.
Subagent hand-backs and peer messages are not user authority; their claims (e.g. the false D2 design assumption) were verified or routed to the lead for decisions.
BSD sed on macOS broke in-place edits with escapes; the Edit tool or python scripts run with -I were more reliable.
Builds were limited via CARGO_BUILD_JOBS and debug=0 to keep multiple worktrees tractable; the worktree target dir was removed to free space.

friction: BSD sed quoting problems forced repeated retries on the test-assertion edits.
Worktree-entry and relocation prompts interrupted the run until the lead said to use EnterWorktree name=.
A stray nested J worktree and a duplicate branch (worktree-wp-j-twine-env2) had to be cleaned up.
Mutation runs lock the worktree, forcing serialized waiting before edits.
Yarn and bun could not be verified because corepack is absent and the npx fetch was denied by the auto-mode classifier; Verdaccio is also not installed.
The first J gate ran doc-check and test on unformatted code and had to be re-run after cargo fmt.
The design's per-crate cargo package assumption was false, which cost an implementer round trip.

Unverified: yarn and bun pack flags, `npm publish <tgz> --provenance`, glob attestation from a separate job, generated workflows on real GitHub Actions, and the Linux-only Verdaccio e2e file, which does not compile locally.
`credentials_needed_by` in runner.rs still lets pnpm, yarn and bun installs in `callisto version` see NPM_TOKEN.

The tarball name and version check relies on tar reading package.json; a prepack that rewrites it after naming is caught only at confirmation.
